summary: The provider charge POST runs inside the @Transactional createInvoiceFromProviderEvent, after the invoice draft is saved and before commit. A rollback, or an SQS redelivery after the charge has been created, cannot reverse the charge; nothing in the path persists the intent or compensates, and the provider call holds the transaction and its connection open while it waits.

evidence.claim: The charge is a POST with side effects at the provider; the body carries no idempotency key, so a retried message can create a second charge.
The remote charge is made inside the open transaction, after the invoice save at line 31.
The transaction boundary encloses the remote call, so a later rollback does not undo the charge.

mitigationsChecked.name: persisted intent
mitigationsChecked.where: InvoiceService.createInvoiceFromProviderEvent (InvoiceService.java:31-35), draft saved in the same transaction

summary: The DTO overload calls the event overload through this, so the proxy never applies and the @Async on the event overload is skipped. The mail send runs synchronously on the HTTP request thread, so SMTP latency or failure is paid by the request, and a failed request retried by a client can send duplicate notices.

evidence.claim: Self-invocation: the DTO overload calls the event overload directly, bypassing the Spring proxy.
The annotation that is bypassed sits on the event overload.
The bypassed method performs the mail send on the calling thread.
The HTTP handler calls the DTO overload, and the controller method carries no @Transactional.

mitigationsChecked.name: self-injected proxy
mitigationsChecked.where: ResidentNotifier constructor (ResidentNotifier.java:13-15), which injects only MailSender

summary: ResidentAccountPortlet is a default-scope singleton, and saveAccount stores each request's query parameter in the instance field lastSearch without synchronization. Concurrent requests from different users overwrite each other's value, and the value differs between replicas. The field is never read in this class, so the damage is a shared, racy value rather than lost work.

evidence.claim: Per-request input is written into a field of a shared singleton bean.
The class declares no @Scope, so it is a default singleton; only @Controller at line 15 applies.

mitigationsChecked.name: synchronized local use
mitigationsChecked.where: ResidentAccountPortlet.saveAccount (ResidentAccountPortlet.java:27-29), no synchronized and no read of lastSearch
